Nxeon hosting platform, Next.js (App Router)/TypeScript, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`).

## The bug (found incidentally by another agent, not yet fixed or deeply investigated)

The `NxMark` component (in `components/marketing/Logo.tsx`) requests an image at path `/icon.png`. Next.js's App Router has a reserved file-based metadata convention: a file at `app/icon.png` (or `app/icon.tsx`/`.ico`/etc.) automatically becomes a special metadata route serving the site's favicon/app-icon at the URL `/icon.png` (actually usually `/icon` or `/favicon.ico` depending on Next version/config — verify the exact reserved path Next.js is generating for this project's `app/icon.png`, since Next sometimes appends a hash or serves it at a slightly different computed path). Whatever `NxMark` is requesting collides with this reserved route, and the resulting request 500s.

## Your task

1. Confirm the exact collision: check whether `app/icon.png` exists (it does, per the other agent's report), find exactly what URL Next.js serves it at (check the built output / route manifest, or just start a dev/build server and curl `/icon.png` to see the actual response — a 500 confirms the collision as reported; also check the Next.js version in `package.json` since the metadata-file route conventions have changed across versions).
2. Find every place `NxMark`/`Logo.tsx` requests `/icon.png` and fix the actual root cause — the real logo mark asset needs its own path that does NOT collide with Next's reserved icon convention. Look at what other logo/brand image assets in this codebase are named and where they live (e.g. `public/` directory conventions) and follow the same pattern — a sensible fix is likely renaming/moving the actual brand-mark image file to something like `public/brand/nx-mark.png` (or wherever similar assets already live) and updating `NxMark`'s reference accordingly. Do NOT rename or remove `app/icon.png` itself if it's legitimately serving the site's real favicon — that's presumably intentional and used correctly elsewhere; the fix is on the `NxMark` component's side, not Next's metadata route.
3. Search the codebase for any OTHER place that might reference the same broken `/icon.png` path (grep for `"/icon.png"` and `icon.png` broadly) to make sure you fix every caller, not just the one instance already found.
4. Verify the fix: after your change, confirm `/icon.png` still correctly serves Next's real favicon (no regression there), and confirm wherever `NxMark` renders now loads its image successfully (no 500, check via a real page load / screenshot if Playwright is available, or at minimum a build + a curl of the new asset path returning 200).

## Build safety

`cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-iconfix -b hotfix/nxmark-icon-collision`, symlink `node_modules`/`.env`, work only there. `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass clean.

This is a straightforward, low-risk, well-contained bug fix (broken image asset causing a 500, not a design or architecture decision) — once verified, follow the established deploy pipeline used elsewhere in this session: commit, merge into `main` via `git merge --ff-only` (reconcile any working-tree conflict by diffing against the worktree's committed version and discarding the redundant uncommitted copy if one exists), sync `/opt/nxeon-staging` (`git fetch && git merge --ff-only origin/main`, `npm run build`, restart `nxeon-staging-web.service`, curl-verify HTTP 200), then run `bash scripts/promote-production.sh` to ship it live. This is safe to take all the way to production without asking first — it's a pure bug fix with no design/product judgment involved.

Report back: what the actual collision was (exact URLs/behavior), the fix, verification evidence, and the final deploy status (commit hash + confirmation production is serving the fix).
